items.title: No monthly local series of doses reached
items.whyItMatters: The June check is one snapshot (61 of 214); without a baseline series the service cannot tell whether the clinic changed anything or the case mix did.
items.opportunity: Build a monthly count of patients at half target dose or more of all indicated classes from the clinic list, starting with the six months before the clinic opens.

items.title: Safety of four-class titration is known only from uncontrolled reports
items.whyItMatters: Potassium holds and kidney function falls are reported from service data without comparison (claims c3, c5), and the pooled trials did not titrate SGLT2 inhibitors.
items.opportunity: Track potassium above 6.0 mmol/L, symptomatic hypotension and eGFR falls above 30 percent as balancing measures reviewed monthly by the clinical lead.

items.title: Missed visits concentrate in deprived and distant neighbourhoods
items.whyItMatters: A clinic that works for patients who can travel may widen the gap in doses reached (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Offer telephone visits with community blood tests from the start and report doses reached and missed visits by deprivation fifth.

items.title: Blood test burden for patients who depend on others for transport
items.whyItMatters: Frequent tests were the main burden reported by patients and may cause drop-out.
items.opportunity: Tell patients in advance how many tests titration needs and use the nearest community site.

errorsFound: The request asks whether to study nurse-led titration before offering it; the retrieved randomised and pooled evidence already answers the effectiveness question, so a new comparative study would repeat it rather than add to it.
reevaluation: The gaps are about local monitoring, safety and access, not about whether nurse-led titration works; they call for a service with a monitoring plan rather than a new study.
summary: Four gaps: no baseline series, safety known only from uncontrolled reports, unequal access and blood test burden.
